summary.title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable, Navigable, and Editable

setting_and_object.category: Mechanism / System artifact (behavior-centric repository representation plus navigation workflow)

details: Evolving an agent harness (prompt construction, state management, tool invocation, execution control) requires first solving 'behavior localization': finding all code sites implementing a behavior described in a natural-language modification request.
Existing repo maps, code search, indexing and memory are implementation-centric (files/functions/modules) and do not expose how a behavior is distributed across execution stages and shared state.

Harness Handbook: a behavior-centric representation auto-synthesized from a codebase, organizing knowledge as an L1 system overview / L2 execution-stage components / L3 source-linked unit entries document tree plus a cross-stage state-register view; every L3 locator must revalidate against current source or is frozen.

Construction pipeline: deterministic static analysis (call graph, signatures, source ranges) provides immutable facts, then LLM-assisted behavioral structuring maps source units onto an execution-stage skeleton, in one of two fixed leaf modes (function-as-leaf from a trusted seed skeleton, or file-as-leaf that infers the skeleton).

Behavior-Guided Progressive Disclosure (BGPD): coarse-to-fine navigation from L1/L2 stages, expanded via the state-register view and call graph, then verified against the live repository to yield source-grounded evidence for an edit plan; every non-empty diff triggers scoped handbook resynchronization.
Terminus-2 (Python terminal agent from Harbor): 6 files, 103 internal functions, 257 resolved call edges; function-as-leaf mode; handbook has 20 stages, 106 L3 entries, 10 state registers.
Codex (Rust monorepo for the Codex coding agent): 2,267 files, 34,363 functions, 159,960 call edges; file-as-leaf mode; handbook has 140 stages, 2,267 L3 entries, 62 registers.
Two harnesses differ by ~2 orders of magnitude in scale, instantiating the two leaf modes.
30 behavior-driven requests per harness, built from shared behavioral intents but phrased against each codebase.
Types: Query (change existing behavior/trigger/timing), Cross-file (add end-to-end capability spanning files/schemas/interfaces), Search-Hostile (sites in mirrored copies, fallback or cold paths).
Also labeled Easy / Medium / Hard by localization difficulty; requests never reveal target locations.
Read-only planner agent built on NexAU with DeepSeek-V4-Pro as LLM; only the edit plan (not execution) is scored.

Baseline: repository exploration with read-only tools (file read, in-file search, directory listing). Handbook-Assisted: same setup plus the handbook exposed as a SKILL.md skill with a BGPD-consistent navigation policy; requests, snapshot, tools, decoding identical.

Plan quality judged by three LLM judges (GPT-5.5, Opus 4.8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro) on Localization (0.5), Scope Control (0.25), Reasoning (0.25); judges first build a leakage-safe answer key from the request and pristine source, then score; win requires >=3-point margin, else tie.
Win rates on the weighted 0-100 plan-quality score, overall and per judge/type/difficulty.
Reference-plan localization: Recall/Precision/F1/Wrong (zero overlap) at file and symbol granularity against independent reference plans from Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5.
Planning cost: average planner tokens per request, including handbook and source context.

key_findings.finding: Handbook-guided localization yields better edit plans while consuming fewer planner tokens.
key_findings.evidence: Overall win rate rose from 28.3% to 38.3% on Codex and 26.7% to 45.6% on Terminus-2, consistent across all three judges (10.0-point gap on Codex; 13.3-26.7 on Terminus-2), while average planner tokens fell from 0.102M to 0.089M per Codex request (-12.7%) and 0.058M to 0.053M per Terminus-2 request (-8.6%).

key_findings.finding: With the handbook, a weaker planner's predicted edit sites align much more closely with reference plans from substantially stronger models.
key_findings.evidence: All 24 Recall/Precision/F1 comparisons (2 harnesses x 2 reference models x file and symbol granularity) improved, with F1 gains of 5.0-18.8 points; on Terminus-2 the handbook arm reached 84.7%/89.3% file-level F1 and up to 93.3% precision against GPT-5.5; precision and recall rose together.

key_findings.finding: Handbook guidance mainly removes complete localization failures rather than merely refining plausible plans.
key_findings.evidence: Wrong (share of requests with zero overlap with the reference) never increased and dropped by up to 25.9 points (Codex symbol-level, 44.4% to 18.5%; file-level 37.0% to 14.8%; Terminus-2 20.0% to 6.7% against GPT-5.5).

key_findings.finding: Gains generalize across request types and difficulty levels, with the largest benefit on scattered, cross-module, and search-hostile changes.
key_findings.evidence: All six harness-by-type comparisons favored the handbook arm by 16.3-33.3 points (Codex best on Query, +26.7; Terminus-2 best on Search-Hostile, +33.3; Cross-file +16.3 and +20.0), and all six harness-by-difficulty comparisons were positive (3.7-33.3 points), non-monotonic in labeled difficulty.

key_findings.finding: The two-mode construction design lets the same behavior representation scale from a tiny Python harness to a large Rust monorepo.
key_findings.evidence: Function-as-leaf (seeded skeleton) produced 106 L3 entries over 6 files for Terminus-2, while file-as-leaf (inferred skeleton, bottom-up rollup from file cards) produced a 140-stage, 2,267-entry handbook for Codex's 34k functions, and both arms yielded improvements under the same BGPD workflow.
